annotations.text:
LEADS — three steps, top to bottom.

1. Choose which businesses: search plus one menu per filter (Priority, Colour, Website…). Every choice shows as a chip under the menus with ✕ to remove it, and the count of what is left.
2. Tick the ones you want — or none.
3. Do something with them: one button opens every action with its price.

• Only what you chose is shown. Columns, widths and buttons never move when a filter changes.
• Colour is a filter like any other; the key sits above the table.
• ICP is the first filter — it is how the list is narrowed to your customers.
• Budget and revenue are visibly off with the reason on hover.

LEADS — one filter menu open.

• Each menu lists its options with how many businesses each gives.
• Show these applies it and adds the chip. Nothing else on the page moves.

LEADS — step 3 open.

• Replaces the old scattered buttons (whole-list actions, ticked actions, paid data for all).
• First: which businesses — the ticked ones or all shown.
• Then: one action, each with its price and who bills it.
• The total sits next to the Start button. Paid data still goes to its own confirm screen.

ONE BUSINESS — split into four tabs so nothing is buried.

• Header: who they are, how to reach them, priority, and every action on this business.
• Full analysis = read site + 51 checks + browser page read + re-score, in that order.
• Overview: why this lead, what to say, and everything known — grouped by source, never a blank.

WEBSITE PAGES tab.

• One card per page read in a real browser: score, checks it failed, the model's read, a line to open the call with.
• Screenshots only for the home and product pages.
• Verdicts follow the checklists, so editing a checklist changes these immediately.

CHECKS & SCORES tab.

• Score by area (higher = more wrong), the biggest problems with evidence, speed.
• Every one of the 51 checks: wrong / fine / could not measure — the last is never counted either way.
• Where every value came from.

CALLS & HISTORY tab.

• Calls so far, with + Log a call. The form is not on the page until you press it.
• Every task ever run on this business, with what it did and cost. Collapsed unless something is running.
LOGGING A CALL — the panel after + Log a call: channel, result, objection, notes. Cancel closes it with nothing saved.

BUY EXTRA DATA — the only screen where money is spent.

• Each kind of data: what it gives, price each × how many = total, who bills it.
• Already bought = free again. Things that cannot be looked up are skipped and counted.
• The source you came for is ticked already.
• Spending limit the run stops at. Warnings in plain words.

DASHBOARD — how the whole list is doing.

• Pipeline left to right, each a subset of the one before.
• Next actions, each with one button.
• Breakdowns are links into the leads list with that filter on.
• What it has cost, by provider.

FIND BUSINESSES — step 1 of a search.

• Type of business, place, radius.
• Nothing is spent here; the next screen shows the cost.

CHECK THE COST — step 2.

• Cost range and number of Google searches, with who bills it.
• Limits: how many businesses, maximum spend.
• What runs afterwards (free).

SEARCH IN PROGRESS — step 3.

• Progress, found, excluded, spend so far, Stop.
• Grid of search circles.
• Failures shown with whether they cost anything.

IMPORT — step 1.

• Choose a CSV. Column names are matched loosely.
• Nothing is added before the preview.

IMPORT — step 2, check before adding.

• New / already in your list (merged, never duplicated) / possible duplicates / could not read, each with reasons.
• What to do after: read & score, sort into categories (free), get Instagram (paid, priced next).
IMPORTED FILES — every list uploaded, with delete.
ONE IMPORTED FILE — what it produced and what it was told to do, with a link to open those businesses in Leads.

ADD ONE BY HAND.

• Name is required; website and phone make everything else possible.
• Honest note: a name alone cannot find the Google listing yet.

INSTAGRAM — the off-site view.

• Who has an account, who has been looked up, followers, category, ads.
• Price the ones not looked up in one step.
• What Instagram will and will not tell anyone.

ICPs — who you actually want to sell to. This replaces Categories completely.

• Each ICP: a name, an industry, the words it is searched by, and what a business must have to count as one.
• Checked top down, first match wins.
• Businesses no ICP describes are kept in one place, not deleted.
• Nothing here costs anything.

ADDING AN ICP — in a panel, like every other form.

• The words are the same ones Find businesses will search Google Maps with, so an ICP is written once and used for sourcing AND filtering.
• Conditions: website, Instagram, followers, reviews, places.
• Budget and revenue are shown but switched off, with the reason on hover.
• Preview says how many businesses it would take, and how many would move.
CHECKLISTS — your rules, and + Add a rule. No form on the page.

CHECKLISTS — adding a rule, in a panel.

• Which pages, which category, what to check, weight, and the sentence to say when it fails.
• Preview on pages already read. Rules can be switched off.
HOW IT WORKS — every rule in plain words, as an accordion. Numbers on this page come from the same settings the product uses.

DATA & SPEND.

• Totals, what is free, every paid source with price and who bills it.
• The ledger of what was actually spent.
• What cannot be bought at any price.
SIGN IN — email and password, with a plain error.

SHARED PIECES — design these once, use everywhere: navigation (open / closed), background tasks (waiting, running, unknown size, done, stopped), messages, hover help, row colours, the three kinds of unknown, buttons, empty state.
